subject: English
passage: Bambusa oldhamii, a bamboo species native to the mountains of Taiwan, is the world's main source of high-strength bamboo fiber. The plant produces a fibrous material called cellulose that is used to make textiles. The stems of Bambusa oldhamii are helpful for the process of making fiber because they have a unique structure that makes it easy to extract cellulose. A system of hollow chambers in the bamboo's stems helps the cellulose to separate cleanly when workers apply steam treatment.
prompt: What feature of Bambusa oldhamii does the text say is helpful for the process of making fiber?

choices.A: Its cellulose produces textiles of an especially high quality.
choices.B: It is able to grow in a wide variety of elevations around the world.
choices.C: It is one of only two bamboo species in Taiwan that produce cellulose.
choices.D: Its stems have a unique structure that makes it easy to extract cellulose.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most accurately states what feature of Bambusa oldhamii is helpful for the process of making fiber. According to the text, this bamboo species produces cellulose, which is used to make textiles, and its stems contain a "system of hollow chambers" that, when treated with steam, enables the cellulose to separate cleanly. The text explicitly states that this feature of Bambusa oldhamii is "helpful for the process of making fiber."
